title: Fifteen Probationers and a Compromise: St Thomas', July 1860
conflicts: Why St Thomas': the London Archives catalogue says Nightingale was drawn by Wardroper's 1855 reforms (Wikipedia, via McDonald, says she chose it for Wardroper and Whitfield), while Monica Baly (1984) argued she hardly knew Wardroper, that the governors made their matron's headship a condition and that Whitfield watered the plan down; the story gives both accounts side by side. Fund: £44,000 (archive), £44,039 (Wikipedia), £45,000 (Baly, Stewart), nearly £50,000 (Guy's and St Thomas'); story says about £44,000. Opening: 9 July 1860 (archive, Wikipedia) against 'due to begin 24 June' (Stewart); story gives 9 July as the records' date. Later service four years (Baly) or at least three (Stewart); no number given. 1,020 nurses by 1900 is Baly's figure only and is attributed to her.
notes: Web search budget ran out during this entry, so research relied on pages already found plus direct fetches (the UKAHN bulletin archive led to Baly's 1984 article, read from its page PDFs). The Dhammapada verse is about evil, applied by analogy to habits formed by early concessions; stance 'complicates'.
